reading: The true table does not beat every blind search in 80% of replicates at any size run, up to 20 times the Indus size (111,681 sign tokens). The permutation test against shuffled tables detects the true table at every size (power 100%, 100%, 100%, 100%, 100%, 100%), so what fails is the comparison with searched tables: a plain blind search finds tables that score above the true one on held-out texts at every size, and the tables it finds read only 3-5% of tokens the way the true table does. With this score, the true table is not what a search maximises, however large the corpus, so scoring below the search ceiling is not evidence against a table and scoring above shuffled tables is not evidence for one.
